correctness.rationale: The crossing-edge inequality forces at least seven selected cubic vertices; equality would induce a perfect matching on an odd seven-vertex shore, so eight is the minimum. The Fano cap and private-point argument gives an exact bijection of all eight-sets with the 84 ordered disjoint Fano triangle pairs. Shared-coordinate pairs reproduce exactly token jumps, identifying the line graph of the Coxeter Kronecker cover; shore-balance forbids slides. Two independent whole-domain 16,384-subset checkers agree, with complete 84-node BFS for diameter seven.

value.rationale: The result turns a recognized domination/majority invariant on the canonical girth-six cubic cage into an exact, meaningful configuration-space identification with Coxeter graph geometry. The ordered-edge bijection explains 84 optima, four possible jump moves from each, complete connectivity and simultaneous slide immobility. This is an informative structural test case for alliance reconfiguration, beyond a routine numeric enumeration.
